<html lang="ko">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>어구독 예비고2 WEEK 01</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/orioncactus/pretendard@v1.3.9/dist/web/static/pretendard.min.css">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:wght@200;300;400;500;600&family=Source+Serif+4:ital,wght@0,400;0,600;0,700;1,400&family=Nanum+Pen+Script&family=Inter:wght@400;600;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>
@page { size: A4; margin: 0; }

html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; background: #fff; }

:root { --ink: #121a33; --navy: #1b2a57; --acc: #ff5a1f; --acc2: #ffb800; --hl: #ffe45c; --gray: #6a6d76; --rule: #d3d6dd; --cream: #fbf7ef; }
.page { width: 210mm; height: 297mm; padding: 12mm 14mm 15mm; position: relative; overflow: hidden; break-after: page; }
.page:last-child { break-after: auto; }
.en { font-family: Inter, Pretendard, sans-serif; font-size: 9.2pt; line-height: 1.62; letter-spacing: -0.005em; }
.disp { font-family: "Black Han Sans", Pretendard, sans-serif; font-weight: 400; }
.hl { background: linear-gradient(transparent 58%, var(--hl) 58%); }
.tip { font-family: "Nanum Pen Script", cursive; font-weight: 400; color: var(--acc); font-size: 15pt; line-height: 1.15; }
.tip b { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 7pt; letter-spacing: 0.12em; color: #fff; background: var(--acc); padding: 0.6mm 1.6mm; border-radius: 1mm; margin-right: 2mm; vertical-align: 1.5pt; }
/* running head */
.run { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 7.4pt; color: var(--gray); margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.run .brand { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.run .brand i { font-style: normal; color: var(--acc); }
.foot { position: absolute; left: 14mm; right: 14mm; bottom: 8mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); }
.foot .pg { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
/* part head */
.part { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: end; column-gap: 4mm; padding-bottom: 2.5mm; border-bottom: 2pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.part .no { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 44pt; line-height: 0.8; color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1.4pt var(--navy); }
.part .no.fill { color: var(--acc); -webkit-text-stroke: 0; }
.part .ttl .e { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 18pt; color: var(--navy); line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.01em; }
.part .ttl .k { font-size: 9.6pt; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-top: 1.2mm; }
.part .meta { text-align: right; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); line-height: 1.35; }
.part .meta .time { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; color: var(--acc); font-size: 13pt; display: block; }
.qr { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 13mm; height: 13mm; border: 0.8pt dashed #9aa0ab; font-size: 5.8pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: center; line-height: 1.2; margin-left: 3mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.part .meta-wrap { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; }
h3.pt { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 2.5mm; margin: 4.5mm 0 2mm; font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 800; color: var(--ink); }
h3.pt .n { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: #fff; background: var(--navy); font-size: 7.6pt; padding: 0.6mm 1.8mm; letter-spacing: 0.08em; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
h3.pt small { font-weight: 500; color: var(--gray); font-size: 8pt; margin-left: auto; }
.lead { margin: 0 0 3mm; color: #33363d; }
/* 판서노트 표 */
table.note { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.9pt; }
table.note th { text-align: left; font-size: 8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.2mm 1.5mm; }
table.note td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.9mm 1.5mm; vertical-align: top; }
table.note td.k { font-weight: 700; width: 46mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 30mm; }
.blank { display: inline-block; min-width: 18mm; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); text-align: center; color: transparent; }
.ex div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.ok { color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; }
.chk { display: inline-block; width: 3.1mm; height: 3.1mm; border: 0.7pt solid #7d828c; vertical-align: -0.4mm; margin: 0 0.6mm; }
ol.q { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; counter-reset: q; }
ol.q > li { counter-increment: q; position: relative; padding-left: 7.5mm; margin-bottom: 2.1mm; }
ol.q > li::before { content: counter(q); position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.3mm; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
.cols2 { column-count: 2; column-gap: 7mm; column-rule: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
.cols2 > * { break-inside: avoid; }
.c { font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap; }
.ox { float: right; color: var(--gray); font-family: Inter; font-weight: 600; font-size: 8pt; }
.wl { display: inline-block; border-bottom: 0.6pt solid #8b9099; min-width: 30mm; height: 4mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.line { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid #b9bdc5; height: 7mm; }
.passage { margin: 1mm 0 2.5mm; text-align: justify; }
.src { font-family: Inter; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.qhead { font-weight: 800; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; font-size: 9.2pt; }
.qhead .src { margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.opts { font-size: 8.6pt; margin: 0 0 1mm; }
.opts div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.gloss { font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: right; margin-top: -1mm; margin-bottom: 1.5mm; }
.rd { break-inside: avoid; margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.pat { margin-bottom: 4.6mm; }
.pat .f { display: inline-block; font-family: Inter; font-weight: 800; font-size: 9pt; color: #fff; background: var(--ink); padding: 0.6mm 2.2mm; margin-right: 2mm; }
.pat .fk { font-weight: 700; }
.pat .s { margin: 1.6mm 0 0 0; }
.cond { font-size: 8.4pt; color: #333; border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.4mm 0; margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; }
.cond b { color: var(--navy); margin-right: 2mm; }
.bogi { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; padding: 1.6mm 0; border-top: 1pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; word-spacing: 1.5mm; }
.tr { margin-bottom: 2.4mm; }
.tr .no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--navy); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 8.6pt; }
/* voca */
table.voc { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.voc td { padding: 1.35mm 1mm; border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
table.voc td.n { width: 6mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: #a3a8b2; font-size: 7pt; }
table.voc td.w { font-family: Inter; font-weight: 700; width: 33mm; }
table.voc td.b { width: 30mm; }
/* plan */
table.grid { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.grid th { text-align: left; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.4mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 2mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td.no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); width: 10mm; }
.score { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.2fr 1fr 1fr 1.4fr; border-top: 2pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 0.6pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.score div { padding: 1.6mm 2.5mm; border-right: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); height: 13mm; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); }
.score div:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.score b { display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.2pt; }
.key h4 { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 8.6pt; color: var(--navy); margin: 3.4mm 0 1.2mm; letter-spacing: 0.04em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: 0.8mm; }
.key h4 span { font-family: Pretendard; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.key .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6mm 4.5mm; font-size: 8.4pt; }
.key .row b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 8.2pt; margin: 0.6mm 0; }
.key .ls b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
/* cover */
.cover { padding: 0; color: #fff; background: radial-gradient(120% 80% at 75% 35%, #2d3f86 0%, #17214a 45%, #0b1024 100%); }
.cover svg.art { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 210mm; height: 297mm; }
.cover .top { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; top: 15mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 8.6pt; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.cover .pill { border: 0.8pt solid rgba(255,255,255,.75); border-radius: 10mm; padding: 1mm 3.2mm; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .series { opacity: .85; font-weight: 500; }
.cover .title { position: absolute; left: 16mm; top: 30mm; }
.cover .title .over { font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 600; opacity: .9; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
.cover .title h1 { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-weight: 400; font-size: 84pt; line-height: 1.02; margin: 2mm 0 0; letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
.cover .title h1 span { color: var(--acc2); }
.cover .title .sub { margin-top: 4mm; font-size: 13pt; font-weight: 700; display: flex; gap: 3mm; align-items: center; }
.cover .title .sub i { font-style: normal; font-weight: 500; opacity: .8; font-size: 10pt; }
.cover .band { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 64mm; background: #f2ff6b; color: var(--ink); padding: 9mm 16mm 0; }
.cover .band .who { font-size: 9.5pt; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .who b { color: #2440b3; }
.cover .band .slogan { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-size: 33pt; line-height: 1.1; margin-top: 2mm; }
.cover .band .feat { position: absolute; right: 16mm; top: 9mm; text-align: right; font-size: 8.2pt; line-height: 1.75; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .feat span { display: inline-block; background: var(--ink); color: #f2ff6b; padding: 0 2mm; margin-left: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.cover .band .bot { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; bottom: 9mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 8.4pt; font-weight: 700; }
.cover .band .bot span { font-weight: 500; }
.memo { margin-top: 5mm; }
.memo .mh { font-family: "Archivo Black", Pretendard; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: .06em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: .8mm; }
.memo .line { border-bottom: .5pt dashed #c3c7cf; }
table.tf { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.4pt; margin-bottom: 1mm; }
table.tf td { border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.2mm .5mm; }
table.tf td.b { width: 12mm; text-align: right; color: var(--gray); }
.sum { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.6pt; border-top: .5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; }
.pair { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.4pt; row-gap: .5mm; }
.q2 { margin-top: 3mm; }

:root { --brand: #213f93; --navy: #213f93; --tint: #eaf1fb; --tint2: #cfdcf2; --acc: #ff6a2b; --ink: #1a1d26; }
.page { padding: 19mm 16mm 15mm 14mm; }
.en { font-family: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, serif; font-size: 9.7pt; line-height: 1.6; letter-spacing: 0; }
/* header band */
.run { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 11mm; margin: 0; padding: 0 16mm 0 14mm; background: var(--tint); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--brand); }
.run .brand { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; padding: 1.2mm 2.6mm; font-size: 7.4pt; letter-spacing: .08em; }
.run .brand i { color: #ffd36b; }
.cover .run { display: none; }
/* thumb index */
.thumb { position: absolute; right: 0; width: 7.5mm; height: 27mm; background: var(--tint2); color: var(--brand); border-radius: 2mm 0 0 2mm; writing-mode: vertical-rl; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 6.6pt; letter-spacing: .12em; }
.thumb.on { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; }
/* part head */
.part { border-bottom: 1.2pt solid var(--brand); padding-bottom: 2.6mm; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; }
.part .no, .part .no.fill { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 21pt; line-height: 1; color: #fff; -webkit-text-stroke: 0; background: var(--brand); padding: 2.2mm 3mm 2mm; border-radius: 1.6mm; }
.part .ttl .e { color: var(--brand); font-size: 16pt; }
.part .meta .time { color: var(--acc); }
/* section chips */
h3.pt .n { background: var(--brand); border-radius: 1mm; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
/* point boxes */
.box { border: .8pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 2.6mm; margin: 0 0 4mm; overflow: hidden; }
.box > h3.pt { margin: 0 0 2mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.8mm 3mm; }
.box > :not(h3) { margin-left: 3.5mm !important; margin-right: 3.5mm !important; }
.box > :last-child { margin-bottom: 3mm !important; }
/* 판서 빈칸 */
.blank { color: transparent; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); position: relative; min-width: 15mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 40mm; white-space: nowrap; }
table.note td.k { width: 50mm; }
.blank i { position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.5mm; color: var(--acc); font-style: normal; font-weight: 800; font-size: 8pt; }
/* choice box */
.c { white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 600; }
.c b { display: inline-block; border: .7pt solid #8796b8; padding: 0 1.4mm; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: 600; }
.c b + b { border-left: 0; }
/* tables */
table.note th, table.grid th { color: var(--brand); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--brand); background: var(--tint); }
table.grid td.no { color: var(--brand); }
ol.q > li::before { color: var(--brand); font-family: "Archivo Black"; content: counter(q, decimal-leading-zero); }
ol.q > li { padding-left: 8mm; }
.exwrap { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 38mm; column-gap: 5mm; }
.vside { border-left: .6pt solid var(--tint2); padding-left: 3mm; font-size: 7.8pt; line-height: 1.55; }
.vside h5 { margin: 0 0 1.5mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--brand); letter-spacing: .08em; }
.vside div { margin-bottom: 1.2mm; }
.vside div span { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-weight: 600; display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.3pt; }
.score { border-top: 1.4pt solid var(--brand); }
.key h4 { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }
.memo .mh { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }
.foot .pg { color: var(--brand); }
.tip b { background: var(--acc); }
.src { color: var(--acc); }
.cover .band .who b { color: var(--brand); }

.qc { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; column-gap: 7mm; row-gap: 1.6mm; }
.qc > div { position: relative; padding-left: 7mm; }
.qc > div > em { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; font-style: normal; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--brand); font-size: 8.4pt; }
.fillw { display: inline-block; min-width: 16mm; border-bottom: .6pt solid #8b9099; }
.abc { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-size: 8.8pt; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 6mm 1fr 1fr 1fr; row-gap: .4mm; margin-top: 1.5mm; }
.abc span.h { color: var(--gray); font-family: Pretendard; font-size: 7.8pt; }

.key .row { font-size: 7.9pt; gap: 0.3mm 3.6mm; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 7.7pt; margin: 0.3mm 0; }
.key h4 { margin: 2.2mm 0 0.8mm; }
.bogi2 { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; border: .7pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 1.5mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 2mm; word-spacing: 2mm; }

table.note td { padding: 1.3mm 1.2mm; font-size: 8.3pt; }
table.note td.k { width: 40mm !important; }
table.note td.v { width: 33mm !important; white-space: normal !important; }
table.note td.en { font-size: 8.9pt; line-height: 1.45; }
.key .row { font-size: 7.6pt !important; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 7.5pt !important; }
.ta{display:none} .c b.ans{}

html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; background: #fff; }
body { font-family: Pretendard, sans-serif; color: #17181c; font-size: 9.2pt; line-height: 1.5; -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }
:root { --ink: #121a33; --navy: #1b2a57; --acc: #ff5a1f; --acc2: #ffb800; --hl: #ffe45c; --gray: #6a6d76; --rule: #d3d6dd; --cream: #fbf7ef; }
.page { width: 210mm; height: 297mm; padding: 12mm 14mm 15mm; position: relative; overflow: hidden; break-after: page; }
.page:last-child { break-after: auto; }
.en { font-family: Inter, Pretendard, sans-serif; font-size: 9.2pt; line-height: 1.62; letter-spacing: -0.005em; }
.disp { font-family: "Black Han Sans", Pretendard, sans-serif; font-weight: 400; }
.hl { background: linear-gradient(transparent 58%, var(--hl) 58%); }
.tip { font-family: "Nanum Pen Script", cursive; font-weight: 400; color: var(--acc); font-size: 15pt; line-height: 1.15; }
.tip b { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 7pt; letter-spacing: 0.12em; color: #fff; background: var(--acc); padding: 0.6mm 1.6mm; border-radius: 1mm; margin-right: 2mm; vertical-align: 1.5pt; }
/* running head */
.run { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 7.4pt; color: var(--gray); margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.run .brand { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.run .brand i { font-style: normal; color: var(--acc); }
.foot { position: absolute; left: 14mm; right: 14mm; bottom: 8mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); }
.foot .pg { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
/* part head */
.part { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: end; column-gap: 4mm; padding-bottom: 2.5mm; border-bottom: 2pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.part .no { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 44pt; line-height: 0.8; color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1.4pt var(--navy); }
.part .no.fill { color: var(--acc); -webkit-text-stroke: 0; }
.part .ttl .e { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 18pt; color: var(--navy); line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.01em; }
.part .ttl .k { font-size: 9.6pt; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-top: 1.2mm; }
.part .meta { text-align: right; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); line-height: 1.35; }
.part .meta .time { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; color: var(--acc); font-size: 13pt; display: block; }
.qr { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 13mm; height: 13mm; border: 0.8pt dashed #9aa0ab; font-size: 5.8pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: center; line-height: 1.2; margin-left: 3mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.part .meta-wrap { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; }
h3.pt { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 2.5mm; margin: 4.5mm 0 2mm; font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 800; color: var(--ink); }
h3.pt .n { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: #fff; background: var(--navy); font-size: 7.6pt; padding: 0.6mm 1.8mm; letter-spacing: 0.08em; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
h3.pt small { font-weight: 500; color: var(--gray); font-size: 8pt; margin-left: auto; }
.lead { margin: 0 0 3mm; color: #33363d; }
/* 판서노트 표 */
table.note { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.9pt; }
table.note th { text-align: left; font-size: 8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.2mm 1.5mm; }
table.note td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.9mm 1.5mm; vertical-align: top; }
table.note td.k { font-weight: 700; width: 46mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 30mm; }
.blank { display: inline-block; min-width: 18mm; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); text-align: center; color: transparent; }
.ex div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.ok { color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; }
.chk { display: inline-block; width: 3.1mm; height: 3.1mm; border: 0.7pt solid #7d828c; vertical-align: -0.4mm; margin: 0 0.6mm; }
ol.q { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; counter-reset: q; }
ol.q > li { counter-increment: q; position: relative; padding-left: 7.5mm; margin-bottom: 2.1mm; }
ol.q > li::before { content: counter(q); position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.3mm; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
.cols2 { column-count: 2; column-gap: 7mm; column-rule: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
.cols2 > * { break-inside: avoid; }
.c { font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap; }
.ox { float: right; color: var(--gray); font-family: Inter; font-weight: 600; font-size: 8pt; }
ol.q > li:has(.ox)::after { content: ""; display: block; clear: both; }
.wl { display: inline-block; border-bottom: 0.6pt solid #8b9099; min-width: 30mm; height: 4mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.line { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid #b9bdc5; height: 7mm; }
.passage { margin: 1mm 0 2.5mm; text-align: justify; }
.src { font-family: Inter; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.qhead { font-weight: 800; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; font-size: 9.2pt; }
.qhead .src { margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.opts { font-size: 8.6pt; margin: 0 0 1mm; }
.opts div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.gloss { font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: right; margin-top: -1mm; margin-bottom: 1.5mm; }
.rd { break-inside: avoid; margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.pat { margin-bottom: 4.6mm; }
.pat .f { display: inline-block; font-family: Inter; font-weight: 800; font-size: 9pt; color: #fff; background: var(--ink); padding: 0.6mm 2.2mm; margin-right: 2mm; }
.pat .fk { font-weight: 700; }
.pat .s { margin: 1.6mm 0 0 0; }
.cond { font-size: 8.4pt; color: #333; border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.4mm 0; margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; }
.cond b { color: var(--navy); margin-right: 2mm; }
.bogi { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; padding: 1.6mm 0; border-top: 1pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; word-spacing: 1.5mm; }
.tr { margin-bottom: 2.4mm; }
.tr .no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--navy); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 8.6pt; }
/* voca */
table.voc { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.voc td { padding: 1.35mm 1mm; border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
table.voc td.n { width: 6mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: #a3a8b2; font-size: 7pt; }
table.voc td.w { font-family: Inter; font-weight: 700; width: 33mm; }
table.voc td.b { width: 30mm; }
/* plan */
table.grid { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.grid th { text-align: left; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.4mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 2mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td.no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); width: 10mm; }
.score { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.2fr 1fr 1fr 1.4fr; border-top: 2pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 0.6pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.score div { padding: 1.6mm 2.5mm; border-right: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); height: 13mm; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); }
.score div:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.score b { display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.2pt; }
.key h4 { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 8.6pt; color: var(--navy); margin: 3.4mm 0 1.2mm; letter-spacing: 0.04em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: 0.8mm; }
.key h4 span { font-family: Pretendard; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.key .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6mm 4.5mm; font-size: 8.4pt; }
.key .row b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 8.2pt; margin: 0.6mm 0; }
.key .ls b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
/* cover */
.cover { padding: 0; color: #fff; background: radial-gradient(120% 80% at 75% 35%, #2d3f86 0%, #17214a 45%, #0b1024 100%); }
.cover svg.art { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 210mm; height: 297mm; }
.cover .top { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; top: 15mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 8.6pt; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.cover .pill { border: 0.8pt solid rgba(255,255,255,.75); border-radius: 10mm; padding: 1mm 3.2mm; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .series { opacity: .85; font-weight: 500; }
.cover .title { position: absolute; left: 16mm; top: 30mm; }
.cover .title .over { font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 600; opacity: .9; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
.cover .title h1 { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-weight: 400; font-size: 84pt; line-height: 1.02; margin: 2mm 0 0; letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
.cover .title h1 span { color: var(--acc2); }
.cover .title .sub { margin-top: 4mm; font-size: 13pt; font-weight: 700; display: flex; gap: 3mm; align-items: center; }
.cover .title .sub i { font-style: normal; font-weight: 500; opacity: .8; font-size: 10pt; }
.cover .band { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 64mm; background: #f2ff6b; color: var(--ink); padding: 9mm 16mm 0; }
.cover .band .who { font-size: 9.5pt; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .who b { color: #2440b3; }
.cover .band .slogan { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-size: 33pt; line-height: 1.1; margin-top: 2mm; }
.cover .band .feat { position: absolute; right: 16mm; top: 9mm; text-align: right; font-size: 8.2pt; line-height: 1.75; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .feat span { display: inline-block; background: var(--ink); color: #f2ff6b; padding: 0 2mm; margin-left: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.cover .band .bot { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; bottom: 9mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 8.4pt; font-weight: 700; }
.cover .band .bot span { font-weight: 500; }
.memo { margin-top: 5mm; }
.memo .mh { font-family: "Archivo Black", Pretendard; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: .06em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: .8mm; }
.memo .line { border-bottom: .5pt dashed #c3c7cf; }
table.tf { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.4pt; margin-bottom: 1mm; }
table.tf td { border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.2mm .5mm; }
table.tf td.b { width: 12mm; text-align: right; color: var(--gray); }
.sum { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.6pt; border-top: .5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; }
.pair { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.4pt; row-gap: .5mm; }
.q2 { margin-top: 3mm; }

:root { --brand: #213f93; --navy: #213f93; --tint: #eaf1fb; --tint2: #cfdcf2; --acc: #ff6a2b; --ink: #1a1d26; }
.page { padding: 19mm 16mm 15mm 14mm; }
.en { font-family: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, serif; font-size: 9.7pt; line-height: 1.6; letter-spacing: 0; }
/* header band */
.run { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 11mm; margin: 0; padding: 0 16mm 0 14mm; background: var(--tint); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--brand); }
.run .brand { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; padding: 1.2mm 2.6mm; font-size: 7.4pt; letter-spacing: .08em; }
.run .brand i { color: #ffd36b; }
.cover .run { display: none; }
/* thumb index */
.thumb { position: absolute; right: 0; width: 7.5mm; height: 27mm; background: var(--tint2); color: var(--brand); border-radius: 2mm 0 0 2mm; writing-mode: vertical-rl; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 6.6pt; letter-spacing: .12em; }
.thumb.on { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; }
/* part head */
.part { border-bottom: 1.2pt solid var(--brand); padding-bottom: 2.6mm; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; }
.part .no, .part .no.fill { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 21pt; line-height: 1; color: #fff; -webkit-text-stroke: 0; background: var(--brand); padding: 2.2mm 3mm 2mm; border-radius: 1.6mm; }
.part .ttl .e { color: var(--brand); font-size: 16pt; }
.part .meta .time { color: var(--acc); }
/* section chips */
h3.pt .n { background: var(--brand); border-radius: 1mm; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
/* point boxes */
.box { border: .8pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 2.6mm; margin: 0 0 4mm; overflow: hidden; }
.box > h3.pt { margin: 0 0 2mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.8mm 3mm; }
.box > :not(h3) { margin-left: 3.5mm !important; margin-right: 3.5mm !important; }
.box > :last-child { margin-bottom: 3mm !important; }
/* 판서 빈칸 */
.blank { color: transparent; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); position: relative; min-width: 15mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 40mm; white-space: nowrap; }
table.note td.k { width: 50mm; }
.blank i { position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.5mm; color: var(--acc); font-style: normal; font-weight: 800; font-size: 8pt; }
/* choice box */
.c { white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 600; }
.c b { display: inline-block; border: .7pt solid #8796b8; padding: 0 1.4mm; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: 600; }
.c b + b { border-left: 0; }
/* tables */
table.note th, table.grid th { color: var(--brand); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--brand); background: var(--tint); }
table.grid td.no { color: var(--brand); }
ol.q > li::before { color: var(--brand); font-family: "Archivo Black"; content: counter(q, decimal-leading-zero); }
ol.q > li { padding-left: 8mm; }
.exwrap { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 38mm; column-gap: 5mm; }
.vside { border-left: .6pt solid var(--tint2); padding-left: 3mm; font-size: 7.8pt; line-height: 1.55; }
.vside h5 { margin: 0 0 1.5mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--brand); letter-spacing: .08em; }
.vside div { margin-bottom: 1.2mm; }
.vside div span { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-weight: 600; display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.3pt; }
.score { border-top: 1.4pt solid var(--brand); }
.key h4 { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }
.memo .mh { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }
.foot .pg { color: var(--brand); }
.tip b { background: var(--acc); }
.src { color: var(--acc); }
.cover .band .who b { color: var(--brand); }

.qc { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; column-gap: 7mm; row-gap: 1.6mm; }
.qc > div { position: relative; padding-left: 7mm; }
.qc > div > em { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; font-style: normal; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--brand); font-size: 8.4pt; }
.fillw { display: inline-block; min-width: 16mm; border-bottom: .6pt solid #8b9099; }
.abc { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-size: 8.8pt; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 6mm 1fr 1fr 1fr; row-gap: .4mm; margin-top: 1.5mm; }
.abc span.h { color: var(--gray); font-family: Pretendard; font-size: 7.8pt; }

.key .row { font-size: 7.9pt; gap: 0.3mm 3.6mm; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 7.7pt; margin: 0.3mm 0; }
.key h4 { margin: 2.2mm 0 0.8mm; }
.bogi2 { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; border: .7pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 1.5mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 2mm; word-spacing: 2mm; }

table.note td { padding: 1.3mm 1.2mm; font-size: 8.3pt; }
table.note td.k { width: 40mm !important; }
table.note td.v { width: 33mm !important; white-space: normal !important; }
table.note td.en { font-size: 8.9pt; line-height: 1.45; }
.key .row { font-size: 7.6pt !important; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 7.5pt !important; }

/* section chips */
h3.pt .n { background: var(--brand); border-radius: 1mm; }

/* point boxes */
.box { border: .8pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 2.6mm; margin: 0 0 4mm; overflow: hidden; }

.box > :not(h3) { margin-left: 3.5mm !important; margin-right: 3.5mm !important; }
.box > :last-child { margin-bottom: 3mm !important; }
/* 판서 빈칸 */
.blank { color: transparent; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); position: relative; min-width: 15mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 40mm; white-space: nowrap; }
table.note td.k { width: 50mm; }
.blank i { position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.5mm; color: var(--acc); font-style: normal; font-weight: 800; font-size: 8pt; }
/* choice box */
.c { white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 600; }
.c b { display: inline-block; border: .7pt solid #8796b8; padding: 0 1.4mm; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: 600; }
.c b + b { border-left: 0; }
/* tables */
table.note th, table.grid th { color: var(--brand); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--brand); background: var(--tint); }
table.grid td.no { color: var(--brand); }
ol.q > li::before { color: var(--brand); font-family: "Archivo Black"; content: counter(q, decimal-leading-zero); }

.score { border-top: 1.4pt solid var(--brand); }
.key h4 { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }

.tip b { background: var(--acc); }
.src { color: var(--acc); }

.qc { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; column-gap: 7mm; row-gap: 1.6mm; }

ol.q.ex1 { font-size: 8.6pt; line-height: 1.38; }

/* BASIC 두 단 + 판서 칸 */

.panbox { border: .7pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 2.4mm; background-color: #fff;
  background-image: radial-gradient(#c3c6dc .55px, transparent .7px); background-size: 5mm 5mm; background-position: 2.5mm 9mm;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; }

CHAPTER 01 주어와 동사의 수일치
강의 40분

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

동사의 수는 동사 바로 앞 명사가 아니라 진짜 주어가 정한다. 고2는 수식어가 두 겹 이상 겹친다.

01명사 주어 — 겹친 수식어는 모두 괄호로

전치사구 · 분사구 · 관계사절 · 콤마 삽입절이 겹쳐도 모두 괄호로 지우고, 남은 머리 명사에 맞춘다.

동사를 먼저 찾고 → 왼쪽으로 가며 꾸밈말을 ( )로 → 남은 맨 앞 명사가 진짜 주어.

[The impact] (of social media) (on how teenagers form their identities) remains a topic of debate.[ ] 진짜 주어 · ( ) 지울 수식어 · 밑줄 동사
The documents stored in the city archive reveal how the town was rebuilt after the war.
The growing evidence from studies on sleep, which researchers in several countries have collected, suggests that brief afternoon naps can substantially improve learning and memory in students.
동사 앞의 archive · countries가 아니라 documents · evidence가 주어.

02동명사구 · to부정사구 · 명사절 주어 = 단수

-ing · To · That · What · Whether · How로 시작하는 주어 덩어리는 「~하는 것」 하나 → 단수 동사.

주어 모양해석동사
Comparing ~ / To learn ~~하는 것은단수
That / What / Whether / How + S + V~라는 것 / ~하는 것 / ~인지 / ~하는 방식단수
Comparing your own progress with the achievements of classmates who started much earlier tends to discourage most learners and weaken their motivation.
Whether the new policies on renewable energy will actually reduce emissions in the coming decades remains uncertain to many analysts.
덩어리 안의 classmates · decades에 속지 말 것.

03주격 관계대명사 + 동사 — 선행사에 맞춘다

관계사절 안의 동사는 선행사의 수에, 문장 전체 동사는 다시 맨 앞 주어에 — 동사 두 개를 따로 판단.

심화 형태선행사who 뒤 동사
one of the + 복수명사 + who복수명사복수
the only one of the + 복수명사 + whothe only one단수
Researchers who study the habits of successful language learners across a wide range of cultures argue that daily effort ultimately matters more than natural talent or intelligence.
She is the only one of the volunteers who speaks three languages, so she guides most foreign visitors.
who 바로 앞 명사가 아니라 「의미상 꾸밈을 받는 명사」가 선행사.

04부분 표현 — of 뒤 명사에 맞춘다

most · some · half · all · the rest · 분수 · 퍼센트 + of + 명사 → of 뒤 명사의 수에 맞춘다.

주어동사
부분 표현 + of + 단수 · 셀 수 없는 명사단수
부분 표현 + of + 복수명사복수
Nearly two-thirds of the information that teenagers share online is visible to total strangers.

05the number of vs a number of

the number of + 복수명사 → 단수 (「~의 수」) / a number of + 복수명사 → 복수 (「많은 ~」)

The number of students who choose online courses has risen steadily over the past decade.
A number of scientists working on climate models at research centers in Europe and Asia have warned that sea levels may rise far faster than previous projections suggested.

학평·수능 the number of 뒤에 관계사절 · 분사구가 붙어 동사가 멀어진다.

06each · every — 언제나 단수

each · every가 붙은 주어, each of + 복수명사, every A and B → 단수 동사.

Every decision made by the committee members during the first planning meeting was recorded for future reference.
Each of the paintings that the gallery borrowed from private collectors comes with a detailed description.

07상관접속사 · 삽입구 — 누구에게 맞출까

both A and B → 복수 / either · neither · not only … but also → B / A as well as · along with · together with B → A(앞 명사).

형태동사
both A and B복수
either A or B · neither A nor B · not only A but also BB에 맞춤
A, as well as · along with · together with B,A에 맞춤

08시간 · 거리 · 금액 = 단수 / the + 형용사 = 복수

숫자 + 단위를 「양 하나」로 보면 → 단수. the elderly · the wounded 같은 「~한 사람들」 → 복수.

Twenty years is a long time for a small company to survive in a rapidly changing industry.
The elderly who live alone in rural areas often struggle to get adequate medical care.
-s 모양(years)과 단수 모양(elderly)에 속지 말 것.

09There be · 장소 부사구 도치 — 동사 뒤 주어

There be, 장소 부사구가 앞에 나온 도치 문장은 동사 뒤의 주어에 맞춘다.

There are a variety of reasons why some people prefer solitary work to working in teams.
Along the narrow path that leads to the top of the mountain stand hundreds of stone statues made by ancient monks.
There 뒤 주어가 advice · little time 같은 단수 · 셀 수 없는 명사면 There is.

10심화 — 보어 · 분사구 · 부정어 도치

보어(형용사 · 분사구)나 부정어가 문장 앞에 오면 「동사(조동사) + 주어」 → 동사 뒤의 주어에 맞춘다.

앞에 나온 말어순수 기준
Equally important · Hidden behind ~be + 주어be 뒤 주어
Rarely · Never · Littledo/does/did + 주어 + 동사원형do 뒤 주어
Hidden behind the old bookshelves in the library was a small door that nobody had opened for years.
Rarely does a scientist working alone in a laboratory make a discovery that changes an entire field overnight.

학평·수능 도치 + 긴 주어는 29번 어법 단골 — 동사 앞 명사(bookshelves · library)는 주어가 아니다.

11심화 — 한 사람 · 한 개념인 「A and B」 = 단수

and로 이어져도 관사가 하나인 한 사람(the poet and novelist)이나 하나의 개념(trial and error)이면 → 단수.

The acclaimed poet and novelist, who spent most of her life in a coastal village, was finally honored by the nation.
Trial and error, rather than careful planning by experts, often leads to the most significant breakthroughs in science.
The poet and the novelist(관사 둘) = 두 사람 → 복수.

To see how borrowing and lending changes a person’s worldview, consider what the rate of interest does to people’s perception of time. Imagine you are lending to somebody at an interest rate of 10 percent per year for five years. This rate tells us that the money lent has a cost that reflects the risk of you not being repaid and the opportunity cost of not spending that money yourself. The longer the term of the loan, the higher the chance you won’t be paid back because it is further into the future—which by definition is unknowable—and the longer you will have to wait before spending the money yourself. In order to make this worthwhile for the lender, money has to have a price—a cost to the borrower and income to the lender. This price factors in the value of time. To put it another way, a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

Research on cephalopod neurobiology suggests that an octopus possesses roughly five hundred million neurons. What makes this system unusual is where many of those neurons are located. More than half are distributed throughout the arms rather than concentrated entirely in the central brain. Each arm contains networks of nerve cells capable of controlling complex movements and responding to sensory input locally. This means that many actions do not require detailed instructions from the brain itself. Instead, the arms function as highly capable extensions of the nervous system that interact with the environment directly. The suckers lining each arm play an important role in this process. These structures provide strong grip but also detect chemical signals on surfaces they contact. Marine biologists studying octopus behavior have shown that this allows the animal to gather chemical information through touch. In practical terms, an octopus can effectively taste what it touches.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

주어가 동작을 하면 능동태, 동작을 받으면 수동태. 고2는 주어와 동사 사이가 멀고, 준동사의 태까지 묻는다.

01능동 vs 수동 — 주어가 하는가, 당하는가

주어가 동작을 하면 능동, 받으면 수동 be + p.p.. 주어 뒤 관계사절 · 분사구를 걷어 내고 본동사의 태를 판단한다.

능동Volunteers from three neighboring towns clean the polluted wetlands every spring so that migrating birds can rest there safely.
수동The polluted wetlands near the river, which migrating birds rely on every spring, are cleaned by volunteers from three towns.

주의관계사절 안의 동사(rely on)가 아니라 본동사(are cleaned)의 태를 본다.

023형식 → 수동태 (by 생략)

목적어 → 주어 자리, 동사 → be + p.p.(시제는 be동사), 원래 주어 → by + 목적격. 행위자가 막연하면 by 이하는 생략한다.

생략Thousands of tons of plastic waste are thrown into the ocean every day, threatening the survival of countless marine animals and contaminating the seafood that people eat.

Frederick Law Olmsted, known as the father of American landscape architecture, was born in 1822. When Olmsted was young, he often went on trips to the countryside with his father, who loved scenery. At age 14, he was preparing himself to study at Yale College, but he could not enter due to a severe sumac poisoning that damaged his eyesight. Instead of attending a college, he gained experience working as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer. In 1858, he worked with Calvert Vaux and won the design competition for New York City’s Central Park with the “Greensward Plan.” During the Civil War, Olmsted served as General Secretary of the United States Sanitary Commission. Although he passed away in 1903, his sons and successors continued his design philosophy. In 1979, the National Park Service designated his home and office in Brookline, Massachusetts, as a National Historic Site to honor his legacy.

강의 40분

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

강조하고 싶은 말이 문장 앞으로 나오면 주어와 동사의 자리가 바뀐다. 고2는 앞에 나온 말과 주어가 길어진다.

01부정어(구) 도치 — Never · Little · Rarely · Under no circumstances

핵심부정어(구)가 문장 맨 앞에 오면 (조)동사 + 주어 순서. 일반동사는 do · does · did + 주어 + 동사원형.

The manager had never questioned the data → Never had the manager questioned the data
도치Never has the city council approved a budget that set aside so much money for public libraries and community centers.
심화Under no circumstances should visitors touch the paintings displayed in this gallery, even when the security guards are not watching them.

주의Not only가 앞에 오면 앞 절만 도치 — Not only did he win the prize, but he also … (but 뒤는 그대로)

02Only + 부사(구·절) 도치

핵심Only then / Only after ~ / Only by -ing ~ 가 앞에 오면 그 뒤 주절이 「조동사 + 주어」로 뒤집힌다.

도치Only after the engineers had tested the system for several months did the company allow the public to use the new app.
도치Only by comparing data collected from many different regions can scientists predict how the climate will change over the next century.

학평·수능Only after 「절」 안은 그대로, 뒤의 주절만 도치 — had tested … did the company allow

03Not until ~ / Hardly ~ when / No sooner ~ than

핵심Not until A + 조동사 + 주어 + 동사 「A하고 나서야 비로소 ~」. Hardly had S p.p. when ~ / No sooner had S p.p. than ~ 「~하자마자」.

We didn’t see the risk until the report came out → Not until the report came out did we see the risk
도치Not until the final report was published did the public realize how much money had been wasted on the failed project.
심화No sooner had the speaker finished her presentation than dozens of students rushed to the stage to ask her questions.

주의짝을 바꿔 쓰면 틀린다 — No sooner ~ when (×) / Hardly ~ than (×)

04장소 · 방향 부사구 도치 — 동사 + 주어

핵심장소·방향 부사구가 앞에 오면 동사 + 주어. 조동사 do를 쓰지 않고 동사를 그대로 앞으로. 동사의 수는 뒤의 주어에 맞춘다.

보통 어순도치
Several letters written during the war were inside the drawer.Inside the drawer were several letters written during the war.
A narrow path runs along the river.Along the river runs a narrow path.
단수In the center of the square surrounded by cafés and souvenir shops stands a bronze statue of the king who built the city.
복수Beneath the surface of the frozen lake near the research station live tiny organisms that can survive without sunlight for months.

주의동사 앞 명사(lake · station)도, 주어 뒤 관계사절 속 명사도 아닌 동사 바로 뒤 머리 명사에 맞춘다. 주어가 대명사면 도치하지 않는다: Here it comes (○)

05보어 도치 — So + 형용사 / 분사 보어 + 동사 + 주어

핵심보어(형용사 · 분사)가 앞으로 나오면 동사 + 주어. So ~ that 구문이 자주 쓰인다.

도치So convincing was the evidence presented by the defense lawyer that the jury reached a decision in less than an hour.
심화Hidden among the thousands of documents in the national archive were several letters that proved the scientist’s theory was correct.

학평·수능보어 · 분사가 앞이면 동사 + 주어 — 수는 뒤 주어(the evidence → was, several letters → were)

06So / Neither / Nor + 동사 + 주어 — 「~도 그렇다」

핵심긍정에 맞장구는 so, 부정에 맞장구는 neither · nor. 동사는 앞 문장의 동사 종류·시제를 따른다.

앞 문장맞장구
be동사 · 조동사 · have p.p.… and so is he / neither can we / neither have I
일반동사 현재 · 과거… and so does she / neither did they
긍정Teenagers who sleep less than six hours a night have trouble concentrating in class, and so do adults working long night shifts.
부정The first experiment did not support the researchers’ hypothesis about memory, and neither did the second one conducted a year later.

주의neither 뒤에 not을 또 쓰지 않는다: neither didn’t they (×)

07There / Here + 동사 + 주어 + There seem(s) to be

핵심There · Here가 앞에 오면 동사 + 주어. 동사의 수는 동사 뒤의 명사가 정한다. There seem(s) to be · There used to be도 같다.

복수There are a growing number of studies suggesting that regular exercise improves not only physical health but also memory.
단수There seems to be little agreement among experts about how artificial intelligence should be used in schools and hospitals.

주의a number of + 복수명사 → 복수 / the number of + 복수명사 → 단수

08간접의문문 — 의문사 + 주어 + 동사

핵심의문문이 문장 속(목적어·주어)으로 들어가면 의문사 + 주어 + 동사. 의문사가 없으면 if · whether + 주어 + 동사.

How important is sleep? → Few people know how important sleep is.
의문사The survey asked parents how much time their children spent on their phones after finishing their homework each evening.
whetherDoctors are still debating whether the new allergy medicine is safe enough for young children.

학평·수능의문사가 주어면 그대로 「의문사 + 동사」 — Nobody knows what caused the fire. do · does · did가 남으면 틀린 것

09think · believe · suppose + 간접의문문 — 의문사가 맨 앞

핵심Do you think ~? 처럼 생각을 묻는 동사가 있으면 의문사를 문장 맨 앞으로 보낸다.

Who was responsible? → Who do you suppose was responsible?
앞으로What do you think the government should do first to reduce the amount of plastic waste in the ocean?
주어Who do you suppose was responsible for the mistake that delayed the launch of the satellite by three months?

주의Do you know는 의문사가 그대로: Do you know who was responsible? (○)

10such · so · enough · how의 어순

핵심such + a(n) + 형용사 + 명사 / so + 형용사 + a(n) + 명사 / 형용사 + enough / how + 형용사·부사 + 주어 + 동사

We can sometimes assume that the whole will be as good as each of its parts. Suppose, for example, you’re in charge of a startup, and you know that everyone you’ve brought on board is productive and efficient. It might seem logical to assume that, as a result, the startup will be productive and efficient, too ― but this isn’t necessarily true. The fallacy of composition fails to allow for how the different “parts” interact with each other ― if, for example, your efficient administrator and your highly skilled head of IT each assumes the other is in charge of collating prototype test results, then you have a problem. Equally, a unit composed of good people can still be working on a doomed project, and a project composed of good ideas may lack a stable center. When assembling a team with a common goal, always check the overall view as well as the individuals involved.

For each objective probability ― from one percent to 100 percent ― we want to know the subjective probability weight. When we make decisions, do we treat a one-percent chance just like one percent, or like something else? Events that could happen but aren’t likely ― low-probability events ― can be defined as probabilities up to about 25 percent. Low-probability events tend to factor more into decisions than they should. That is, an event that has an objective one-percent chance of occurring could subjectively seem like it has a five-percent chance of occurring. We overestimate the likelihood of these low-probability events. In general, the smaller the probability, the more we overestimate its likelihood. For example, people who play the lottery are often optimistic about winning. However, the odds of a single ticket winning the largest, most popular U.S. lotteries are on the order of one in 175 million.

Many of the barriers to trade exist not because of a lack of markets or customers, but because there are major barriers to getting products to market at competitive prices. Transaction costs are significant for companies ― not only the straight exchange costs, but also the cost of converting, paying, and hedging funds just to pay for the goods and services. 1For each objective probability ― from one percent to 100 percent ― we want to know the subjective probability weight.
각각의 객관적 확률, 즉 1퍼센트부터 100퍼센트까지에 대해 우리는 주관적인 확률의 가중치를 알고 싶어 한다.
2When we make decisions, do we treat a one-percent chance just like one percent, or like something else?
우리가 의사 결정을 할 때, 우리는 1퍼센트의 가능성을 단순히 1퍼센트로 취급하는가, 아니면 다른 것으로 취급하는가?
3Events that could happen but aren’t likely ― low-probability events ― can be defined as probabilities up to about 25 percent.
일어날 수는 있지만 그럴 것 같지 않은 사건들, 즉 낮은 확률 사건들은 대략 25퍼센트까지의 확률로 정의될 수 있다.
4Low-probability events tend to factor more into decisions than they should.
낮은 확률 사건들은 그래야 하는 것보다 더 크게 의사 결정에 반영되는 경향이 있다.
5That is, an event that has an objective one-percent chance of occurring could subjectively seem like it has a five-percent chance of occurring.
즉, 객관적으로 1퍼센트의 발생 가능성을 가진 사건이 주관적으로는 5퍼센트의 발생 가능성을 가진 것처럼 보일 수 있다.
6We overestimate the likelihood of these low-probability events.
우리는 이러한 낮은 확률 사건들의 가능성을 과대평가한다.
7In general, the smaller the probability, the more we overestimate its likelihood.
일반적으로, 확률이 더 작을수록 우리는 그것의 가능성을 더 과대평가한다.
8For example, people who play the lottery are often optimistic about winning.
예를 들어, 복권을 사는 사람들은 당첨되는 것에 대해 흔히 낙관적이다.
9However, the odds of a single ticket winning the largest, most popular U.S. lotteries are on the order of one in 175 million.
그러나 가장 규모가 크고 가장 인기 있는 미국 복권에 단 한 장의 표가 당첨될 가능성은 1억 7,500만 분의 1 정도이다.

강의 40분

한 문장에서 본동사는 주어의 동작 · 상태를 말하고, 준동사(to-v · -ing · p.p.)는 명사 · 형용사 · 부사 역할을 한다. 고2는 수식어 · 삽입절이 길어 본동사가 멀리 있다.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

01한 절에 본동사는 하나

핵심접속사 없이 본동사는 하나. 나머지 동사 모양(to-v · -ing · p.p.)은 준동사다.

동사The research team collected soil samples from twenty farms across the region and analyzed them to measure the level of chemical pollution.
준동사The committee met again last Friday to review the safety guidelines proposed by engineers after the accident at the chemical plant.

주의and · but · or로 이은 동사는 앞 동사와 모양을 맞춘다(병렬): collected … and analyzed

02동사 수 = 접속사 · 관계사 수 + 1

핵심접속사 · 관계사가 하나면 동사는 둘. 생략된 that · 목적격 관계사도 센다.

The theory (that) most experts accepted → is now being challenged → that 1개 + 1 = 동사 2개
관계사The theory that most experts accepted until recently is now being challenged by a new generation of young researchers.
생략Many economists argue the rapid rise in housing prices over the past decade reflects a serious shortage of affordable homes in large cities.

학평·수능that이 생략되면 「명사 + 명사 + 동사」가 이어진다 — 앞 동사는 절 안, 뒤 동사가 본동사.

동사원형Reduce food waste at home is easier than most people think.×

The Industrial Revolution did more than just invent new materials or machines. It invented a new process for manufacturing: the modern factory. Prior to around 1850, most piano shops used an apprentice system ① in which a master builder taught younger workers the skills of the trade, usually over the course of many years. The larger piano shops ② did have specialists — for example, one person ③ who specialized in soundboards, another who made hammers, and so on. But even the largest piano makers of that time ④ producing no more than 5-10 pianos per year per worker, as pianos were still made essentially one at a time. The development of a true piano factory occurred first in the United States, ⑤ led by Jonas Chickering in Boston and later the Steinway family in New York City. These factories led to improvements in both efficiency and quality. For example, one of the factories of the time had its own iron casting facility where it made its metal plates, which were thought to be the best available.

The renowned British philosopher Alfred North Whitehead asserted that “civilization ① advances by extending the number of operations we can perform without thinking about them.” Take, for example, the “advance” offered to civilization by the discount coupon, which allows consumers ② assuming that they will receive a reduced purchase price by presenting the coupon. The extent to which we have learned to operate mechanically on that assumption ③ is illustrated in the experience of one automobile-tire company. Mailed-out coupons that ― because of a printing error ― offered no savings to recipients ④ produced just as much customer response as did error-free coupons that offered substantial savings. The obvious but instructive point here is that we expect discount coupons to do double duty. Not only do we expect them to save us money, we also expect them to save us the time and mental energy ⑤ required to think about how to do it. In today’s world, we need the first advantage to handle pocketbook strain; but we need the second advantage to handle something potentially more important ― brain strain.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

to부정사는 「to + 동사원형」, 동명사는 「동사원형 + -ing」. 고2는 준동사가 긴 수식어 속에 숨고, 가목적어 it · 완료형 · 수동형까지 나온다.

01to부정사 — 명사 역할 (주어 · 보어 · 목적어) + 가목적어 it

핵심「~하는 것, ~하기」. 긴 to-v 주어는 가주어 It ~ to-v로 뒤로 보낸다. 5형식 목적어 자리의 to-v는 가목적어 it: find · make · think + it + 형용사 + to-v.

To finish the report by Friday seemed impossible → It seemed impossible to finish the report by Friday
가주어It is important to check the expiration date on any medicine before you give it to young children with a fever.
심화Many first-year students find it difficult to manage their own schedules without the guidance of their parents and teachers.

주의make possible to-v (×) → make it possible to-v (○) — 가목적어 it을 빼먹은 오답이 단골

02to부정사 — 형용사 역할 (명사 뒤에서 꾸밈)

핵심「~할 (명사)」. 명사 뒤에서 꾸미고, 동사가 자동사면 전치사까지: a topic to talk about. decision · ability · chance · attempt 뒤에는 to-v.

수식The government’s decision to raise the price of public transportation caused strong complaints from students and elderly citizens.
전치사Young people who move to a big city for work often struggle to find an affordable apartment to live in.

주의a pen to write (×) → a pen to write with (○) / the ability to adapt (○) · the ability of adapting (×)

03to부정사 — 부사 역할 (목적 · 감정의 원인 · 판단 · 결과)

핵심동사 · 형용사 · 문장 전체를 꾸민다. 가장 많이 나오는 것은 목적 「~하기 위해」, 고2는 결과의 only to-v까지.

쓰임해석예
목적~하기 위해saved money to buy a laptop
감정의 원인~해서shocked to hear the news
판단의 근거~하다니careless to leave it there
결과(결국) ~하다hurried home, only to find it empty
목적To reduce traffic in the city center, the local government has introduced a fee for cars that enter during rush hour.
결과The young inventor worked on the design for years, only to find that a larger company had already registered a similar device.

학평·수능문장 앞 「To-v ~, 주절」은 「~하기 위해」. 동사원형으로 시작하게 바꾼 오답이 단골.

04동명사 — 명사 역할 (주어 · 목적어 · 보어 · 전치사의 목적어)

핵심「~하는 것」. 주어면 수식어가 길어도 단수 동사, 전치사 뒤에는 to-v가 아니라 동명사.

05to부정사만 목적어로 — 앞으로 할 일

핵심바람 · 계획 · 결심 · 시도처럼 미래를 향한 동사는 to-v를 목적어로 쓴다.

to-v만 쓰는 동사
want · hope · wish · plan · decide · expect · agree · refuse · promise · manage · afford · fail · tend · seek · intend
decideAfter weeks of discussion, the school board decided to extend the library’s opening hours until ten.
refuseSome patients refuse to take the medicine prescribed by their doctors because they fear its side effects.

학평·수능decide · plan · refuse · fail · tend 뒤 -ing는 단골 오답.

06동명사만 목적어로 — 이미 하는 일 · 경험

핵심즐기기 · 피하기 · 끝내기 · 인정하기처럼 이미 하고 있거나 해 본 일을 나타내는 동사는 -ing를 목적어로 쓴다.

-ing만 쓰는 동사
enjoy · avoid · mind · finish · keep · consider · suggest · deny · admit · give up · put off · postpone · practice · quit · resist
avoidMany people avoid discussing politics at family gatherings because they want to keep the peace.
admitThe company finally admitted making a mistake in the design of its new battery.

주의suggest to go (×) → suggest going (○) / deny to take (×) → deny taking (○)

07둘 다 쓰지만 뜻이 다른 동사

핵심to-v는 앞으로 할 일, -ing는 이미 한 일. stop · try는 뜻 자체가 달라진다.

동사+ to-v+ -ing
remember · forget~할 것을~한 것을
regret~하게 되어 유감이다~한 것을 후회하다
stop~하기 위해 멈추다~하는 것을 그만두다
try~하려고 애쓰다시험 삼아 ~해 보다
과거The witness clearly remembered seeing a black car parked in front of the bank shortly before the robbery happened.
유감We regret to inform you that the concert scheduled for this Saturday has been canceled because of the singer’s illness.

학평·수능regret to inform · tell · say = 「~하게 되어 유감이다」(공지 · 편지 단골). remember · forget은 시점 단서로.

The city square is a fairly future-proof technology, as is the shopping street, even in an age of online shopping. For example, the same physical store that once sold buggy whips and typewriters might now repair damaged phones and sell bubble tea. The same infrastructure supports evolving uses. Jane Jacobs, the great prophet of the city economy, made much of this fact in her books, including The Death and Life of Great American Cities and The Nature of Economies. As she pointed out, the great advantage of a city architecture is  , and Jacobs correctly predicted the persistence of the city itself, unlike those who predicted the rise of the Internet would mean the death of the city.

분사는 동사에서 나온 형용사. 꾸밈을 받는 명사가 동작을 하면 -ing, 당하면 p.p. 고2 지문은 분사구가 길어 본동사가 멀리 있다.

01현재분사 vs 과거분사 — 하는가, 당하는가

핵심명사가 스스로 하거나 진행 중이면 -ing(능동·진행), 당하거나 끝난 상태면 p.p.(수동·완료).

-ing (능동·진행)p.p. (수동·완료)

-ingThe rising cost of housing in large cities has forced many young workers to move to the outskirts and spend more than two hours commuting every day.

주의falling leaves(떨어지는 잎) / fallen leaves(떨어진 잎) — 뜻이 달라진다.

02분사의 자리 — 한 단어면 앞, 구면 뒤

핵심분사 한 단어는 명사 앞, 목적어 · 부사구가 붙은 분사구는 명사 뒤에서 꾸민다.

Psychotherapist Fran Weller describes grief work as “an act of devotion, rooted in love and compassion” that requires “an ongoing practice of deepening, attending and listening.” When we grieve for what is lost, it clears the way towards a strengthening of love and commitment for what remains. In time this may build a desire to make good from the loss by repairing as many damages as we can and/or compensating for them. Grief can make us both very sad and  .

When we focus on the obvious aspects of media, we miss  . Most of us notice the obvious aspects of a new medium or technology while missing the more subtle aspects. Take, for example, the microwave oven. It was introduced in the early 1980s and revolutionized food preparation. Traditionally, one person spent the better part of an afternoon fixing an evening meal for a family. Now, it was possible to prepare foods very quickly, and this shortening of preparation time was liberating for the cooks in the family, most of whom tended to be women. But the short-term, obvious implications of greater convenience made it easy to overlook the long-term implications of no longer having one person fix food for the family to eat together at an evening meal. As time went on, fewer and fewer families sat down together to eat dinner. Meals that took a long time to prepare became a luxury of the past, except perhaps for special occasions. The effects of the microwave oven on family life were not anticipated and would have been difficult to foresee.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

준동사(to부정사 · 동명사 · 분사)에도 행위자 · 시간 · 태가 있다. 고2는 긴 수식어 속에서 의미상 주어 · 완료형 · 수동형이 겹쳐 나온다.

01to부정사의 의미상 주어 — for + 목적격

핵심to부정사의 행위자가 문장 주어와 다르면 to 앞에 for + 목적격을 쓴다. 가주어 It 구문 · too ~ to · enough to에서 자주 나온다.

It is essential + for new employees + to learn the safety rules
forIt is essential for new employees to learn the safety rules before they are allowed to operate the heavy machines in the factory.
tooThe instructions in the manual for the new washing machine were too technical for most elderly customers to follow without help from their children or grandchildren.

주의행위자가 일반 사람(we · people)이거나 문장 주어와 같으면 for ~를 쓰지 않는다.

02사람의 성격 형용사 — of + 목적격

핵심kind · considerate · wise · careless · foolish · rude · generous처럼 사람의 성격을 말하는 형용사 뒤에는 of + 목적격.

형용사의미상 주어
important · mandatory · difficult · necessary · naturalfor + 목적격 (일에 대한 판단)
kind · considerate · wise · careless · foolish · rude · generousof + 목적격 (사람에 대한 판단)
ofIt was considerate of the hotel staff to prepare a birthday cake for the elderly guest who was traveling alone.
ofIt was foolish of the company to ignore the complaints that customers had posted online for months.

학평·수능「It is + 형용사 + [for / of] + 목적격 + to-v」 — 형용사가 일을 평가하는지, 사람을 평가하는지로 고른다.

03동명사의 의미상 주어 — 소유격(목적격)

핵심동명사의 행위자가 문장 주어와 다르면 동명사 앞에 소유격을 쓴다. 일상 영어에서는 목적격도 쓴다.

소유격The residents strongly objected to the city council’s building a waste treatment plant so close to the elementary school.
목적격Nobody in the office could have imagined the shy intern becoming the most successful salesperson in the company.

주의주격(he · they) + -ing는 틀린다: they being late (×) → their being late (○)

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

관계사 = 앞 명사(선행사)를 꾸미는 절을 여는 말. 고2는 선행사와 관계사 사이가 벌어지고, 전치사 · 수량 표현이 붙어 나온다. 그래도 열쇠는 뒤 절이 완전한지 · 불완전한지.

01관계대명사 = 접속사 + 대명사

핵심선행사가 사람이면 who, 사물·동물이면 which, 둘 다 that. 뒤 절에는 주어나 목적어가 하나 빠져 있다.

격사람사물 · 동물둘 다
주격whowhichthat
목적격who(m)whichthat
소유격whosewhose (of which)—
사람The engineer who designed the new bridge was praised for considering both safety and the beauty of the river.
사물The vaccine which the research team developed last year has already been approved in more than thirty countries.

주의뒤 절에 빠진 성분이 없으면 관계대명사 자리가 아니다.

02주격 관계대명사 + 동사 — 수는 선행사에

핵심who · which · that 바로 뒤 동사의 수는 선행사에 맞춘다. 선행사 뒤에 전치사구가 끼면 그 앞 명사가 선행사.

복수Patients who follow the doctor’s advice about diet and exercise usually recover faster than those who ignore it.
단수The report on rising sea levels that was released by the government last month alarmed many environmental experts.

학평·수능「one of the + 복수명사 + who」 — 선행사가 복수명사라 관계사절 동사도 복수.

03목적격 관계대명사는 생략할 수 있다

핵심목적격 who(m) · which · that은 생략 가능 → 「명사 + 주어 + 동사」가 바로 붙는다.

the theory (that) the scientist proposed = the theory the scientist proposed
생략The theory the young scientist proposed at the conference was later supported by several independent experiments.
생략Much of the food we throw away every day could feed families in regions suffering from serious shortages.

주의주격은 생략하지 않는다. 단, 「주격 + be동사」는 함께 생략할 수 있다: the data (which were) collected last year.

핵심that은 선행사 있음, what은 선행사 포함(= the thing which). 둘 다 뒤 절은 불완전.

핵심뒤 절이 불완전하면 관계대명사, 완전하면 관계부사(where · when · why · how).

선행사관계부사= 전치사 + which

핵심「전치사 + which · whom」 뒤에는 완전한 절. 전치사는 뒤 절 동사 · 형용사의 짝(depend on · be interested in)으로 정한다.

08계속적 용법 — , which / , who

핵심콤마 뒤 관계사는 「그런데 그것은 · 그 사람은」으로 이어 읽는다. which는 앞 절 전체도 받는다.

The team lost the final, which disappointed its fans. → which = 결승에서 진 일
명사The festival takes place in Andong, which is known for its traditional houses and mask dance performances.
절 전체The company decided to cut its budget for research, which worried many of the younger engineers.

학평·수능「, that」 「, what」은 무조건 틀린 표현. 앞 절 전체를 받는 which 뒤 동사는 단수.

09that을 주로 쓰는 자리 · 못 쓰는 자리

핵심선행사에 the only · the very · 최상급 · all · everything이 있으면 주로 that. 전치사 뒤 · 콤마 뒤에는 that 불가.

onlyMr. Lee was the only teacher that noticed the shy student’s remarkable talent for drawing during her first semester.
allAll that the visitors could see from the top of the tower on that cold morning was a thick layer of gray fog covering the whole city.

주의「전치사 + that」, 「, that」은 쓰지 않는다.

10복합관계사 — -ever

핵심whoever = anyone who(~하는 누구든), whatever = anything that(~하는 무엇이든), wherever = 어디서 ~하든.

whoeverWhoever wants to join the debate team must submit a short essay on the control of online games by Friday.
whateverThe new manager promised to do whatever she could to improve working conditions and job satisfaction in the factory, where workers had complained about long hours.

주의whoever는 사람, whatever는 사물. whoever가 주어인 절의 동사는 단수(wants).

11심화 — 수량 표현 + of + whom · which

핵심some · many · most · all · none · both + of + whom(사람) · which(사물)이 콤마 뒤에서 절을 잇는다. 대명사 them을 쓰면 접속사가 없어 틀린다.

I have two cousins, both of whom live in Busan. ↔ , both of them live (×) → , and both of them live (○)
whomThe robotics club has over fifty members, most of whom joined after watching its performance at the school festival.
whichThe local museum displays dozens of ancient coins, some of which were discovered by children playing near the river.

학평·수능「, most of them」 vs 「, most of whom」 — 앞에 and가 없으면 whom · which.

When self-experimentation and conventional experiments are both possible, the difference between them often resembles the difference between learning and showing: Self experiments are better for discovery but worse for convincing others that the solution is helpful or the answer is correct. Of course, most scientists want to do both — discover something and convince others of their discovery. Thus, psychologists should consider doing both self-experiments and conventional ones. The best use of resources may often be self-experiments followed by conventional ones. The researcher begins with self-experiments that, if all goes well, find large effects and/or generate and eliminate many hypotheses. This exploratory and theory-building phase lasts until a convenient solution or large effect is found. Then the researcher uses self-experiments to find the procedural parameters (e.g., duration, time of day, intensity) that optimize the solution or maximize the effect. Only then would the researcher begin conventional experiments, using the optimized parameters.

The brain needs to create a model of a constant pulse ― a schema ― so that we know when the musicians are not conforming to it. This is similar to variations of a melody: We need to have a mental representation of what the melody is in order to know ― and appreciate ― when the musician is taking liberties with it. Metrical extraction, knowing what the pulse is and when we expect it to occur, is a crucial part of musical emotion. Music communicates to us emotionally through systematic violations of expectations. These violations can occur in any domain ― the domain of pitch, rhythm, tempo, and so on ― but occur they must. Music is organized sound, but the organization has to involve some element of the unexpected or it is emotionally flat and robotic. Too much organization may technically still be music, but it would be music that no one wants to listen to.

Dolphins’ brains have evolved specialized areas dedicated to echolocation, allowing them to process acoustic information more quickly and with less energy. One key adaptation is the structure of the dolphin’s auditory pathway. The signals from the ears are rapidly transmitted to the auditory cortex, the brain region responsible for processing sound. However, unlike many other mammals, dolphins have a highly specialized auditory cortex with distinct areas dedicated to processing different aspects of echolocation signals. Some areas may be responsible for analyzing the timing of echoes, while others focus on the frequency content or the intensity of the sound. This specialization allows the dolphin’s brain to process echo information in parallel, rather than sequentially. Imagine a factory assembly line, where different workers are responsible for different tasks. By dividing the work among specialized areas, the brain can process information much faster and more efficiently. This parallel processing reduces the cognitive load associated with echolocation, allowing dolphins to react quickly to changes in their environment.

종류대표 단어
물질 · 추상information · advice · evidence · knowledge · research · feedback
집합적 사물furniture · equipment · luggage · machinery · scenery
불가산The questionnaire provided useful feedback on how students in remote areas use online resources to prepare for exams.
단수All of the medical equipment ordered for the new rehabilitation center was delivered safely last month.

주의two evidences (×) → two pieces of evidence (○)

02수량 형용사 — few / little, a number of / a great deal of

핵심복수명사 앞 (a) few · many · a number of, 셀 수 없는 명사 앞 (a) little · much · a great deal of. a 없으면 「거의 없는」.

셀 수 있는 명사셀 수 없는 명사
약간 있는a few complaintsa little evidence
거의 없는few complaintslittle evidence
많은many · a number ofmuch · a great deal of
fewFew of the residents at the town meeting believed that the new highway would reduce traffic jams.
littleThe committee paid little attention to the complaints of local farmers about the new water tariffs.

학평·수능a great deal of는 셀 수 없는 명사 앞에만, a number of는 복수명사 앞에만 쓴다.

03재귀대명사 — 주어와 목적어가 같을 때

핵심같은 절의 주어 = 목적어면 -self / -selves. 절이 달라지거나 가리키는 사람이 다르면 him · them 같은 목적격.

재귀Athletes who push themselves too hard during the off-season often suffer fractures that keep them out of important competitions.
목적격The new manager asked her team members to tell her honestly what they thought about the proposed changes to the schedule.

주의관용: by oneself 혼자서 · for oneself 스스로 · pride oneself on ~을 자랑으로 여기다

04대명사의 수 — 가리키는 명사에 맞춘다

핵심대명사는 가리키는 명사의 수를 따른다. 관계사절 · 분사구가 끼어도 앞에서 찾는다.

단수The government, criticized for its slow response, announced that it would provide substantial subsidies to flood victims.
복수Many teenagers trust online influencers because they seem more like close friends than distant celebrities.

핵심보어 자리(be · become · seem · remain · prove · sound · feel · taste · keep · make · find)는 형용사, 동사 · 형용사 · 분사 · 문장을 꾸미면 부사.

The plan sounded reasonable (보어)↔The plan was carefully reviewed (분사 수식)
보어Despite the heavy rain, the volunteers remained cheerful and kept cleaning the polluted beach all afternoon.
부사The new drug was quickly approved by the authorities after medical trials showed that it was highly effective.

주의remain · prove · stay 뒤 부사 함정: remain calmly (×) → remain calm (○)

10so vs such · -thing + 형용사

핵심such (a) + 형용사 + 명사, so + 형용사 / 부사. -thing · -one은 형용사가 뒤에서 꾸민다.

The concept of “choice architecture,” (a) popularized in behavioral economics, highlights how the design of the environment in which choices are made can significantly influence the decisions people make. Algorithms are, in essence, (b) sophisticated architects of our digital environments. By curating what we see, what we are recommended, and what options are presented to us, they subtly, and sometimes not so subtly, nudge us towards particular paths. While nudges can be used for (c) beneficial purposes, such as encouraging healthier habits, they also carry the potential for manipulation, particularly when the underlying objectives of the architects are not aligned with the well-being or autonomy of the individual. The question then becomes: how can we cultivate and protect our human agency in an increasingly algorithmic world? It requires a conscious effort to maintain critical engagement with the technologies we use. It means actively seeking out diverse perspectives, (d) accepting algorithmic recommendations, and making deliberate choices that go against the predicted grain. It involves cultivating a healthy (e) skepticism towards the seemingly objective outputs of algorithms and remembering that these systems are designed by humans with specific goals, and that their data is a reflection of past realities, not necessarily a prescription for future flourishing.

It is crucial to recognize that boredom can give rise to (a) harmful emotions such as depression, despair, and irritation if not adequately addressed. When we believe that the only way to be happy is by searching for fun activities, then we become (b) dependent on those activities, and negative thoughts and emotions arise. It is suggested that ‘Idle time is the devil’s workshop’ implies that those with too much time on their hands may fill that time with troubling thoughts and behavior. The balance is to not see it as idle time, wasted time, or boredom but rather as a perfect time for self-improvement, self-identification, and positive reflection time. Reflecting, just how lucky are we to be bored? Boredom doesn’t exist in the (c) absence of danger, as it is only an indulgence pastime in a safe zone. Boredom can be perceived as a luxury that typically manifests in (d) safe and inactive situations, presenting an occasion to appreciate and comprehend the environment. In hazardous circumstances, the luxury of boredom is unavailable. Thus, it is paramount to utilize idle moments for profound self-reflection. It represents an occasion to listen, observe, and (e) appreciate before expressing. Rather than viewing boredom as unproductive, it should be regarded as an opportunity for personal development and constructive contemplation.

02비교급 + than — 비교 대상을 맞춘다

야생 생물이 관리되는 수많은 방법들이 있지만, 그것들은 모두 관리 책임을 수반하며 적극적 관리와 소극적 관리라는 두 가지 넓은 범주로 분류될 수 있다.
2Active management does something to the population — such as increasing or decreasing its size — in a direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, respectively.
적극적 관리는 거주지 이전이나 사냥 같은 전략을 통해 각각 개체군의 크기를 늘리거나 줄이는 것처럼 개체군에 직접적인 방식으로 어떤 일을 한다.
3Populations can also be actively managed by altering the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population.
개체군은 또한 서식지를 개체군에 유리하게 또는 불리하게 바꿈으로써 적극적으로 관리될 수 있다.
4If population numbers are too low for the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated, such as predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement to provide required cover for neonates from predators.
개체 수가 관리 기관의 목표에 비해 너무 적으면, 갓 태어난 개체의 죽음을 최소화하기 위한 포식자 통제나 갓 태어난 새끼들에게 포식자로부터 필요한 은신처를 제공하기 위한 서식지 개선 같은 다른 적극적 관리가 포함될 수 있다.
5These efforts represent active approaches to management.
이러한 노력들은 관리에 대한 적극적인 접근법을 나타낸다.
6In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, which often involves management of humans and not animals.
그러한 상황에서 관리 활동은 개체군과 서식지에 대한 외부의 영향을 최소화하는데, 그것은 흔히 동물이 아니라 인간에 대한 관리를 포함한다.

강의 40분

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

조동사는 말하는 사람의 확신 · 후회 · 의무를, 가정법은 사실과 반대인 상상을 나타낸다. 고2 지문은 시점 단서(yesterday · now)가 다른 절이나 앞 문장에 있다.

01추측의 조동사 — must · may · can’t

핵심강한 추측 must(~임에 틀림없다), 약한 추측 may / might(~일지도 모른다), 강한 부정 추측 can’t(~일 리 없다).

mustEvery seat in the lecture hall was taken an hour before the talk, so the guest speaker must be a highly respected expert in child psychology.
can’tThe signature on the confidential contract can’t be the director’s, because she was attending a pharmaceutical conference in Tokyo that entire week.

주의「~일 리 없다」는 mustn’t가 아니라 can’t. mustn’t는 「~하면 안 된다」(금지).

02조동사 + have p.p. — 과거에 대한 추측 · 후회

핵심지나간 일을 지금 추측하거나 후회할 때는 조동사 뒤에 have p.p.를 쓴다.

형태뜻
must have p.p.~했음에 틀림없다
may(might) have p.p.~했을지도 모른다
can’t have p.p.~했을 리 없다
should have p.p.~했어야 했는데 (안 했다)
need not have p.p.~할 필요가 없었는데 (했다)
추측The streets are covered with broken branches and fallen roof tiles, so a devastating storm must have passed through the town while we were asleep.
후회The company should have tested the software more rigorously before releasing it to millions of users around the world.

학평·수능yesterday · last night처럼 과거 표현이 있으면 「조동사 + 동사원형」이 아니라 「조동사 + have p.p.」

03주장 · 요구 · 제안 + that + S + (should) 동사원형

핵심insist · demand · suggest · recommend · order · require 뒤 that절이 「해야 한다」는 내용이면 (should) 동사원형. 부정은 (should) not + 동사원형.

제안The environmental committee recommended that the factory reduce its use of plastic packaging by half within the next three years to meet stricter regulations.
요구The hospital requires that every visitor to the intensive care unit wear a mask and wash their hands thoroughly.

주의that절이 「사실」이면 시제대로: The test results suggested that the patient had been exposed to the virus weeks earlier.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ②

04used to · would · be used to -ing

핵심과거의 습관·상태는 used to(상태 O), 과거의 반복 동작은 would(상태 X), 「~에 익숙하다」는 be used to -ing.

상태There used to be a quiet fishing village where the huge container port now stands on the southern coast.
동작Every winter, my grandmother would knit thick sweaters for all of her grandchildren while listening to old radio programs.

주의be used to -ing = ~에 익숙하다 ↔ be used to 동사원형 = ~하는 데 쓰이다(수동): The barn is used to store grain.

05had better · would rather · may as well

핵심뒤에는 모두 동사원형. 부정은 had better not · would rather not.

충고You had better not rely on a single website when you collect data for your research paper, because online information is not always accurate or up to date.
선택Many employees would rather work from home two days a week than receive a small pay raise that barely keeps up with inflation.

주의had not better (×) → had better not (○) / would rather A than B에서 A·B는 같은 동사원형.

06가정법 과거 — 지금 사실과 반대

핵심If + S + 과거형(be는 were), S + would / could + 동사원형. 해석은 「(지금) ~라면 …할 텐데」.

현재If the subway ran later at night, fewer students would have to take expensive taxis after their evening classes.
wereIf I were in charge of the school cafeteria, I would offer more vegetarian dishes.

학평·수능주절에 would + 동사원형이 보이면 if절은 과거형. 단순 조건(If it rains, …)과 구별.

07가정법 과거완료 — 과거 사실과 반대

핵심If + S + had p.p., S + would / could + have p.p. 해석은 「(그때) ~했더라면 …했을 텐데」.

과거If the engineers had inspected the bridge more carefully last year, they would have noticed the structural cracks in its supports before heavy trucks began to cross it.
부정If the volunteers had not arrived with sandbags that night, the flood would have destroyed most of the houses in the village.

주의if절에 would를 쓰지 않는다: If the engineers would have inspected (×)

08혼합 가정법 — 과거 일이 지금에 영향

핵심If + S + had p.p.(과거), S + would + 동사원형(지금). 주절에 now · today가 단서.

혼합If I had taken the job offer in Singapore five years ago, I would be living abroad with my family now.
혼합If the government had invested in solar energy a decade ago, the country would rely much less on imported oil and face a smaller trade deficit today.

학평·수능앞은 ago · last year, 뒤는 now · today — 두 절의 시점이 다르면 혼합 가정법.

09I wish · as if

핵심I wish / as if + 과거형 = 주절과 같은 때 사실의 반대, + had p.p. = 그보다 앞선 때 사실의 반대.

wishI wish I had kept a diary during my trip to Peru, because I have already forgotten many of the details.
as ifThe novelist describes the ancient city as if she had walked through its streets herself, although she never visited it.

주의주절이 과거(looked · wished)여도 같은 때면 과거형, 앞선 때면 had p.p.: He looked as if he had not slept for days.

10If 생략 도치 — Were · Had · Should

핵심If를 빼면 동사가 주어 앞으로 간다: If I were → Were I / If he had known → Had he known / If you should need → Should you need.

원래If 생략
If I were you, …Were I you, …
If she had known, …Had she known, …
If you should have questions, …Should you have questions, …
HadHad the pilot not reacted so quickly to the engine failure, the plane would have crashed into the hills near the airport during the emergency landing.
ShouldShould you have any questions about the requisite documents for the scholarship, please contact the admissions office before the end of May.

학평·수능「Had + S + p.p.」로 시작하면 주절은 would have p.p. 부정은 Had + S + not + p.p. (Hadn’t he ×)

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ④ 고2 심화

11심화 — It is essential · necessary that + S + (should) 동사원형

핵심「꼭 필요하다 · 중요하다」 형용사(essential · necessary · vital · important) 뒤 that절도 (should) 동사원형.

원형It is essential that every driver check the tire pressure before setting out on a long journey, especially when heavy snow and frost are expected on mountain roads.
원형The surgeon said it was necessary that the patient remain in the hospital for another week of observation.

주의insist · suggest가 「사실」을 전하면 시제대로: The driver insisted that the light had been green when he entered the intersection.

12심화 — 가정법 대용: Without · But for · It is time

핵심Without / But for + 명사 = If it were not for(지금) · If it had not been for(그때). It is (high) time + S + 과거형 = 진작 했어야 할 일.

형태시점
Without ~, S + would + 동사원형(지금) ~이 없다면 = If it were not for ~
Without ~, S + would have p.p.(그때) ~이 없었다면 = If it had not been for ~
It is (high) time + S + 과거형이제 ~해야 할 때다
WithoutWithout the support of local volunteers, the small library would have closed during the financial crisis of 2008.
timeIt is high time the city replaced the old water pipes that have been leaking for more than a decade.

학평·수능Without 문장의 시점은 주절 동사로 판단: would + 동사원형 = 지금, would have p.p. = 그때.

1Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been.여러분을 일상적인 틀에서 벗어나게 하는 사건들을 생각해 보라. 아마 가족 결혼식에 참석하거나, 중요한 발표를 하거나, 한 번도 가 보지 못한 곳에 가는 일 같은 것들 말이다.
2It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged.시간이 조금 느려지는 것 같고 여러분이 더 온전히 몰입한다고 느끼는 것은 바로 그런 때이다.
3The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing.등산이나 패러세일링처럼 그 경험이 위험한 경우에도 마찬가지이다.
4Your senses are sharper. You notice more.여러분의 감각은 더 예민해진다. 여러분은 더 많은 것을 알아차린다.
5Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings.도파민이라고 불리는, 기분을 좋게 하는 화학 물질이 뇌에서 분비되는 덕분에, 여러분은 계획된 만남보다 사람들과의 우연한 만남에서 더 크게 몰려오는 즐거움을 얻는다.
6Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises.좋은 소식, 금전적 보상, 그리고 선물은 뜻밖의 것일 때 더 즐겁다.
7It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.그것이 가장 인기 있는 텔레비전 프로그램과 영화가 예기치 않은 줄거리 반전과 놀라운 결말을 가진 것들인 이유이다.
